model_location.claim: Claude runs on Anthropic's service; the selected environment changes tool execution location, not model location.

tool_execution_location.claim: Built-in bash and file tools execute in an isolated Linux container managed by Anthropic for the session.

environment_custodian.claim: Anthropic operates the sandbox; the application selects the environment and configures its network rules and packages.

context_egress.claim: Conversation history, tool results, sandbox files/state, skills and memory stores are available to the Managed Agents service; web search and fetch execute on Anthropic's side.

tool_surface.claim: The documented surface includes bash, file operations, web search/fetch and configured MCP servers; the exact enabled tools are agent configuration.

provider_identity.claim: Session event history and workflow/thread lifecycles expose provider identities; none is an owner work or acceptance identity.

retry_and_completion.claim: A repeated result for the same custom tool call has no further effect at the session API. Workflow/thread failures and missing thread output still require explicit owner-side treatment; provider terminal status is not work acceptance.

cancellation_and_interruption.claim: A session interrupt stops the agent turn but does not itself end open workflow runs; ask the agent to stop its runs or wait for their ended events. A budget pause is a separate state.

usage_and_cost.claim: Session events expose cumulative usage and tracked list cost; a session budget stops new model requests at its list-cost ceiling. This is not target-effect cancellation or a local per-work-item settlement record.

effect_authority.claim: A provider session grants no estate effect authority. Any effect is limited by the target owner's credential, operation and current decision.

unknowns: The selected model/version, account-specific data controls, configured tools, network policy and credentials vary by agent and environment and are not established by this source map.
No provider session or owner-side event replay was run for this activity.

model_location.claim: Claude and the agent loop remain on Anthropic's side; the worker executes bash and file tool calls on the operator's infrastructure.

tool_execution_location.claim: Tool commands and file operations run on the self-hosted worker; web search/fetch and MCP server connections remain service-side.

environment_custodian.claim: The operator owns worker hardening, network limits, isolation and environment-key handling.

context_egress.claim: Conversation history, tool results, skills and memory stores reach Managed Agents; sandbox files/processes stay on the worker, but tool results sent to the model cross to Anthropic.

tool_surface.claim: The worker executes bash/file calls; the self-hosted option omits managed file/GitHub session resources. Web search/fetch and MCP server connections remain service-side.

provider_identity.claim: Provider session/workflow/thread IDs identify provider execution and must be linked to the estate's separate work and attempt IDs.

retry_and_completion.claim: Same-call result replay is idempotent at the documented session endpoint; this does not establish exactly-once worker effects or owner acceptance.

cancellation_and_interruption.claim: Session interrupt does not end open workflow runs. The operator owns worker/process cleanup in addition to requesting the agent stop its runs; exact worker termination evidence is not established here.

usage_and_cost.claim: Session usage and list-cost budgets are provider-side; actual worker compute, account billing and per-owner-task allocation require separate operator evidence.

effect_authority.claim: Self-hosting changes tool execution location, not model or effect authority. A target owner still controls credentials and accepts effects under its own contract.

unknowns: The worker's actual hardening, egress rules, mounted credentials and deployment state require operator evidence.
No provider session or owner-side event replay was run for this activity.

model_location.claim: OpenAI operates the Codex harness, model/tool loop, session orchestration, compaction and recovery; the exact configured model remains an agent setting.

tool_execution_location.claim: Shell, code and file work runs in an OpenAI-provisioned sandbox; application function tools still execute in the application server.

environment_custodian.claim: OpenAI provisions and manages the hosted sandbox; the application supplies task inputs and configures packages, files, network access and available tools.

context_egress.claim: Session input/events and tool results are exchanged with the OpenAI-managed harness. Exact retention and each tool's data flow depend on the configured API and tools.

tool_surface.claim: The hosted environment runs shell/code/file work; the agent may also use application function tools, MCP and configured hosted tools.

provider_identity.claim: These identify API resources or one pending tool/approval action; they are not a work item, attempt or acceptance identity.

retry_and_completion.claim: The API exposes session and tool-call lifecycle. The reviewed sources do not establish exactly-once delivery or make a terminal session state an owner acceptance.

cancellation_and_interruption.claim: The API accepts a cancel-turn event. A hosted environment can outlive a session; reconcile any external effect and verify environment cleanup independently.

usage_and_cost.claim: Model usage, OpenAI tools and OpenAI-hosted containers have separate API, tool and container rates; account totals and task-level allocation still require source evidence.

effect_authority.claim: Configured function tools run in the application and hosted tools/sandboxes run within their documented boundary; none substitutes for the target owner's credential, operation and current decision.

unknowns: Selected model, organization data controls, environment contents, network policy and tool credentials are deployment-specific.
No provider session or owner-side event replay was run for this activity.

model_location.claim: OpenAI operates the model/tool-loop harness and durable session; the application operates the connected executor environment.

tool_execution_location.claim: The application starts and connects an executor that runs requested commands in its selected environment; application function tools run wherever the application implements them.

environment_custodian.claim: The application/operator manages executor setup, connection, environment lifecycle and private-network access.

context_egress.claim: Tool results and agent context return to the OpenAI-managed harness; the executor can keep its filesystem local, but returned content crosses the provider boundary.

tool_surface.claim: The configured self-hosted executor runs requested commands; application function tools run in their application implementation and MCP tools use their configured server boundary.

provider_identity.claim: API resource and call IDs must be joined to a separate estate work/attempt mapping; executor identity is additional provenance.

retry_and_completion.claim: The reviewed sources do not promise exactly-once executor effects. Ambiguous executor results require owner-side reconciliation before retry; session completion is not acceptance.

cancellation_and_interruption.claim: A cancel-turn event stops current model work; the application manages executor lifecycle and must separately stop or reconcile already-issued tool work and pending effects.

usage_and_cost.claim: Model and OpenAI tool rates are provider-side; self-hosted compute and its cost remain application/operator responsibilities. No local per-work-item cost source is established here.

effect_authority.claim: The application controls executor credentials and tools, while the target owner controls the effect contract and acceptance. Provider IDs confer neither.

unknowns: Actual executor identity, network routes, credentials, failure recovery and data retention require deployment-specific qualification.
No provider session or owner-side event replay was run for this activity.

placements.product: OpenAI Agents SDK (Python, local function tools)
placements.environment_variant: Application process and configured model provider

model_location.claim: The SDK supports configured model providers; model location is determined by the selected provider, not by the SDK session object.

tool_execution_location.claim: Local function tools execute in the application process; hosted OpenAI tools execute on OpenAI servers; other tool types follow their configured runtime.

environment_custodian.claim: The application owns the local process and locally implemented tools; provider-hosted tools and any sandbox retain their own execution boundary.

context_egress.claim: Model inputs and outputs cross to the configured model provider. Tool inputs/results may also be traced; tracing sensitivity is configurable. Tool-specific egress must be reviewed separately.

tool_surface.claim: This placement covers local FunctionTools; the SDK also provides hosted OpenAI tools, and ShellTool can be local or hosted. The configured tool type decides execution location.

provider_identity.claim: SDK sessions are client-managed history; Responses conversation/response IDs are provider-managed continuation; trace/group IDs are observability links. None alone is an owner work identity.

retry_and_completion.claim: The SDK can resume interrupted runs and retain conversation history, but application tools own their own idempotency and a completed run is not domain acceptance.

cancellation_and_interruption.claim: The SDK exposes interruptions and resumable run state, but cleanup/cancellation of a currently executing local tool depends on the application runtime and tool implementation.

usage_and_cost.claim: The SDK reports per-run aggregated usage and per-request entries; provider pricing and local tool/compute costs require separate source records.

effect_authority.claim: The application tool and target owner define effect permissions and acceptance; an SDK session, trace or model response grants no effect authority.

unknowns: Actual model provider, tool registry, approval policy, tracing configuration and target credentials are application-specific.
No provider session or owner-side event replay was run for this activity.

qualification_scenarios.scenario: Replay one provider event or tool-call result after losing the consumer acknowledgement.
qualification_scenarios.required_owner_invariant: The same event and owner idempotency key reconcile to one durable observation/effect. A distinct event is not deduplicated only because its payload matches.

qualification_scenarios.scenario: A parent workflow finishes while a child thread/result is absent or unreadable.
qualification_scenarios.required_owner_invariant: Keep the missing child in the expected coverage denominator; outcome and acceptance remain unknown until owner evidence closes the gap.

qualification_scenarios.scenario: A child tool/model call fails while the parent emits a terminal summary.
qualification_scenarios.required_owner_invariant: Preserve the child failure and its evidence; a parent summary or provider terminal state cannot override the owner's acceptance criteria.

qualification_scenarios.scenario: A replaced or interrupted worker returns after a newer attempt owns the work.
qualification_scenarios.required_owner_invariant: Bind the result to its originating attempt and artifact revision; retain it as evidence without settling or overwriting the current owner state.

limitations: This source map records documented product boundaries, not current account settings, runtime deployment or paid qualification.
The scenario list is a fixture contract only. It is not evidence that an owner implementation passed those cases.
No provider terminal event, session/thread ID or run trace is an owner acceptance or effect receipt.
